label: try T55, a labelled in-sample diagnostic, never an adoption result: M1 (with R1, R2 and g_mom's factors, the entry's form) with its Feng direction split into the part all cell groups share (c) and the group-specific parts (s_g) as try T51 makes them, the parts sized apart at the step and twice the step, on T44's and T46's routes (both E10.5 cuts, the chamber cut also library by library); the cuts are ones earlier T1 choices were made on; the result can only go to the team captain
choices: Off M a form keeps the entry's own values (NaN or a held gene, which M1 does not move), so that the forms differ from the entry on M only.

A group's moved genes are zone_read.moved_mask's (d_g finite and the gene not in M1's held list), the same definition as try T51's per-group mask; M is split_read.common_mask of them and c, s_g split_read.split_vectors' (c the unweighted mean over every direction group).
Where a group's moved genes are not M, or sum(c d_g) is not positive in a group, the run stops before any build and writes no task file; the read is then void with the truth missing.

Statement 2's 'worse' reads 'the common part alone scores worse at equal movement'; 'mixed' is printed with the two comparisons' labels. Statement 3 uses the same wording with 'equal projection' and is read by nothing.

Statement 3's same-size multiple is per group: sqrt of the form's recorded squared size ratio for m1_r_gmom_cp and twice it for m1_r_gmom_cp_x2, the uniform arms' gain over the pooled arm of the arm's fraction by zone_read.size_alone (linear between 1, 1.5 and 2), 'outside the uniform arms' elsewhere.
a_n,g, a_p,g and the (1, 1) deviation are compared between the five files exactly (one computation on the same inputs); the (1, 1) check is the largest absolute difference from d_g on M per group.
Labels on each library truth: T46's single-task test of each arm against its comparison arm (ahead, behind, level).

After review, Statement 1's labels are per arm ('dropping them', 'halving them', '1.5 times them' scores better or worse) in place of the brief's shared labels, which called a gain of the arm that adds the parts 'dropping them scores better' and claimed content ('they carry part of the score') for arms whose size differs too.
The centred figures (a_n on centred vectors, each form's centred squared size ratio) are taken over M with the mean over M removed, and are read by nothing.
limits: One released day, in-sample, on cuts earlier choices were made on.
'Equal movement' is equal squared size of the direction over the moved genes, not equal counts moved or equal change in expression.
c is a mean of four directions in which the endocardial cells count twice, and it holds a quarter of each group's own direction.
The released day's low share along the specific parts (try T51) may be a slower pace of what separates cell types on this one day and says nothing about the two days of the test.

Larger steps score better on these cuts and how far depends on the truth's depth (tries T50 and T54), so an arm that moves more than its comparison arm can gain by size alone, and no outcome sets a size at the test.
The two fractions share the seeds, the draw and the directions, so agreement at both is one result read twice; 'both' is never two confirmations.

An arm that moves less than its comparison arm can lose by size alone: Statement 1's arms differ from m1_r_gmom in content and squared size together (their ratios are printed), so Statement 1 is not size-controlled and is descriptive; Statement 2 is its size-controlled form.
s_g is not orthogonal to c within a group: dropping or scaling it also changes how far the arm moves along c (the recorded 2 sum(c s_g)/sum(d_g^2)).

Equal movement is the uncentred squared size; a constant log offset over the moved genes is largely removed by M1's depth rescaling and moves cells little, so cn can carry less effective movement than the entry where c holds such an offset (the centred ratios are printed beside, read by nothing).

'Better' in Statement 2 means the moved cells land closer along the day's change on these cuts, not that the group-specific parts are noise or biologically empty; the read cannot separate noise in s_g from a different pace of s_g (try T51's limit).

'No difference at the bar' is not 'no difference': with ten seeds on one draw, in-sample cuts and the 0.3 bar, an effect below the bar or within one cut's noise can hide; the per-seed ranges are printed.

Statement 3: a_p,g >= a_n,g (Cauchy-Schwarz), so the cp form's squared size ratio is at least 1 and m1_r_gmom_cp_x2's same-size multiple 2 a_p,g / a_n,g is at least 2: it is outside the uniform arms by construction (on their edge only where c is parallel to d_g), not as a data outcome.
